proof_summary: For \(2\le n\le4\), a congruence modulo \(3^n\mid81\) combining the weighted digit sums of a number and its reversal forces its digit sum to be \(3^n\), hence it has exactly \(3^{n-2}\) digits, all equal to 9. For \(n\ge5\), repeating the 11-digit palindromic block \(29799999792\) exactly \(3^{n-5}\) times gives a smaller palindrome divisible by \(3^n\): the block supplies \(3^5\), and a geometric-sum factor supplies the remaining power of 3.
